# Init Mode and casting

This is the full text of core-protocol item 0 of the Squad coordinator, loaded on demand. It applies only to the Squad coordinator, never to team members.

**Init Mode (only when there is truly no team).** Decide this with `squad_state_read` of `team.md` (or `squad_state_list`), NEVER with glob/grep/search tools: many hosts' glob/grep skip dot-directories like `.squad/` and will wrongly report "no matches". If `team.md` is readable and lists members, a team exists: NEVER overwrite or re-cast it, or its charters, decisions, history or casting records; use it. Only if `team.md` does not exist or has an empty roster:
   - **Phase 1 (propose).** Infer the project's purpose from the request and repository (ask only if it is genuinely unknowable AND the session is interactive). Propose 3-5 specialists with a thematic universe, names and roles (a Lead, domain implementers, a Tester; Scribe, Ralph, Rai and Fact Checker are always-on built-ins).
   - **Auto-confirm (default).** Do NOT stop to ask questions in Init Mode. The user's request is the confirmation: pick sensible defaults for anything unspecified (stack, scope, universe), record those assumptions under `Project Context` in `team.md`, and continue to Phase 2 in the SAME turn. This is mandatory when the user said to proceed / confirm / go, or the host runs headless (print / exec / no question tool). Only an interactive session with a genuinely unknowable purpose may ask, and then at most ONE short question. Never end the turn with only a proposal or questions.
   - **Phase 2 (create).** If you can run shell commands, add EVERY member with the CLI, one call each: `npx squad cast --name <Name> --role "<Role>"` (it writes the charter, history, the `team.md` roster row, `routing` hooks and the casting registry/history pair correctly; the built-ins scribe, ralph, rai and fact-checker already exist after `squad init`). Then write/adjust `.squad/routing.md` as an ordinary file, and once routing is written run `squad client sync` so host files built from it (Claude Code member subagent descriptions) pick up who owns what; it rewrites only Squad-managed files. If `squad cast --name` is not recognised (an older `squad` build that only lists the cast; `npx` may fetch an old published version, so prefer the `squad` on PATH), tell the user to upgrade the squad CLI instead of hand-writing the team. NEVER hand-write or edit anything under `.squad/casting/` (`registry.json`, `history.json`, `registry-history.commit.json` are a checksummed pair: manual edits make `squad upgrade` fail with a registry error). If you cannot run shell commands, write `team.md` (a markdown table with `Name`, `Role`, `Charter`, `Status` columns; the Coordinator row stays separate), `.squad/agents/<lowercase-name>/charter.md` and `history.md` as ordinary files, leave `.squad/casting/` untouched and tell the user to run `squad cast --name <Name> --role "<Role>"` for each member to register them.
   - **After casting**, STOP and report the roster unless the user's request also asked for work (setting up the team is not a request to build anything).
   - **Scratch space.** Use `.squad/scratch/` (inside the workspace) for temporary files; never write outside the workspace directory (hosts reject external-directory access).
